leverage.exposure: An open leveraged position is live and it outranks everything else in this briefing. The offer on Makengo exceeds available cash, nobody else has bid on the listing, and because the offer already tops the asking price it wins by default unless it is withdrawn. The auction resolves roughly two hours before the matchday lock, which is a real buffer but a thin one to be relying on. Three outcomes exist and only two are acceptable: fund it by selling Bernardo, or withdraw the offer. The third — doing nothing — is not a smaller version of the other two, it is a total loss of the matchday, and it is what happens by default. The premium already committed on that offer is above market value and, on an uncontested listing, was more than it needed to be; that is a lesson for the next bid, not a reason to unwind this one. Withdrawing and re-placing lower would reopen a full day of exposure to a rival, and under a points objective the premium is sunk and the cash has no competing use this matchday.

binding_gap: There is no shortage of bodies and no formation hole — the constraint is cash, not shape. Georg can field a legal eleven now and will still be able to after the swap. What binds is that the outstanding offer is larger than the balance behind it, so the squad cannot absorb the incoming player without a sale first. That is the whole of the gap, and one instant sale closes it.

verdict.headline_short: One thing matters this run and it is unchanged from the last one: the
verdict.detail: One thing matters this run and it is unchanged from the last one: the live Makengo offer is leveraged and must be funded or withdrawn before it resolves tomorrow afternoon, roughly two hours before the matchday lock. Doing neither is the default if Georg does nothing, and it means a negative balance at matchday start and zero points for the whole of MD2. Sell Bernardo back to Kickbase — it is instant, needs no counterparty and pays exactly market value. Do it tonight rather than relying on tomorrow's narrow window. Everything else this run is quiet: no squad player is hurt, nothing on the board earns a bid, and no flip clears its cost.

sell.reason: Bernardo is the sale, and the case for it is funding, not football. He is a verified probable starter at left-back for Hoffenheim against Dortmund — four dated sources this week put him there with Hranac absent from the eleven — so this gives up real points to gain more. The Kickbase buy-back is instant and pays exactly market value, which is what makes it the only funding route that does not depend on finding a willing buyer inside a day. One timing refinement: his market value is ticking upward and updates tonight, so selling after tonight's update rather than before fetches a little more for a few hours of waiting, and still leaves a wide margin before the deadline. Do not list him above market value chasing a manager premium — Georg's own Amoako listing just lapsed unsold doing exactly that. The alternative funding route of selling Widmer and Lokonga instead reaches a worse eleven and is barred anyway, because Lokonga is a keeper.

buy.reason: Nothing new on the board earns a bid. Two listings appeared since the last run and both were rejected on their merits rather than on price. Irie is the one worth naming: a Freiburg midfielder, cheap, rising, with a respectable-looking average — but he is not in Freiburg's dated probable eleven for the weekend and his average is a single game off bench minutes, which is the exact trap of a good number bought from a player who does not play. He is also unaffordable once the Makengo funding lands without a third sale. Uno is a summer signing with no points history at all and a falling value; a small price tag is Kickbase's floor valuation, not a bargain, and the man behind it has produced nothing. The rest of the board is already covered by standing avoids. Makengo himself is verified fit and starting, and the offer stands.
